subject.title: Feature Request: Cron Job Hooks System

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class persisted cron hook/gate API for pre/post/onError behavior, and if so should it be job-owned config, plugin-owned runtime hooks, or a narrower command-gate feature?
rationale: The missing behavior is real, but it creates public cron config/protocol surface and unattended shell/webhook execution semantics that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor scoped hook design
options.body: Define a narrow persisted lifecycle/gate API with a security model and then implement it across cron runtime, protocol, CLI/UI, docs, and tests.

options.title: Narrow to existing command jobs
options.body: Declare command payloads plus current plugin hooks sufficient for now and close or split hook-specific requests into smaller follow-ups.

options.title: Extend plugin hooks instead
options.body: Keep per-job config lean and add only the generic plugin/runtime hook capability needed to gate or observe cron runs safely.

recommendation.title: Sponsor scoped hook design
recommendation.body: Define a narrow persisted lifecycle/gate API with a security model and then implement it across cron runtime, protocol, CLI/UI, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He already gave the concrete cross-surface review on this issue and is the strongest routing candidate for the product/security boundary choice.
